5.bsb: Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, “We have seen remarkable things today.”

5.web: After these things he went out, and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow me!”
5.kjv: And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me.
5.bsb: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him,

5.web: He left everything, and rose up and followed him.
5.kjv: And he left all, rose up, and followed him.
5.bsb: and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.

5.web: Levi made a great feast for him in his house. There was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining with them.
5.kjv: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them.
5.bsb: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.

5.web: Their scribes and the Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?”
5.kjv: But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners?
5.bsb: But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus’ disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”

5.web: Jesus answered them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.
5.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick.
5.bsb: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

5.web: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
5.kjv: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
5.bsb: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”

5.web: They said to him, “Why do John’s disciples often fast and pray, likewise also the disciples of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?”
5.kjv: And they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink?
5.bsb: Then they said to Him, “John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.”

5.web: He said to them, “Can you make the friends of the bridegroom fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
5.kjv: And he said unto them, Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?
5.bsb: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?

5.web: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days.”
5.kjv: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.
5.bsb: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.”

5.web: He also told a parable to them. “No one puts a piece from a new garment on an old garment, or else he will tear the new, and also the piece from the new will not match the old.
5.kjv: And he spake also a parable unto them; No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agreeth not with the old.
5.bsb: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.

5.web: No one puts new wine into old wine skins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and it will be spilled, and the skins will be destroyed.
5.kjv: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.
5.bsb: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.

5.web: But new wine must be put into fresh wine skins, and both are preserved.
5.kjv: But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.
5.bsb: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.

5.web: No man having drunk old wine immediately desires new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
5.kjv: No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.
5.bsb: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”

6.web: Now on the second Sabbath after the first, he was going through the grain fields. His disciples plucked the heads of grain and ate, rubbing them in their hands.
6.kjv: And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.
6.bsb: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.

6.web: But some of the Pharisees said to them, “Why do you do that which is not lawful to do on the Sabbath day?”
6.kjv: And certain of the Pharisees said unto them, Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days?
6.bsb: But some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”

6.web: Jesus, answering them, said, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, he, and those who were with him;
6.kjv: And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him;
6.bsb: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

6.web: how he entered into God’s house, and took and ate the show bread, and gave also to those who were with him, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?”
6.kjv: How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?
6.bsb: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”

6.web: He said to them, “The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”
6.kjv: And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
6.bsb: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

6.web: It also happened on another Sabbath that he entered into the synagogue and taught. There was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
6.kjv: And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.
6.bsb: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.

6.web: The scribes and the Pharisees watched him, to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, that they might find an accusation against him.
6.kjv: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day; that they might find an accusation against him.
6.bsb: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.

6.web: But he knew their thoughts; and he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Rise up, and stand in the middle.” He arose and stood.
6.kjv: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.
6.bsb: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.

6.web: Then Jesus said to them, “I will ask you something: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?”
6.kjv: Then said Jesus unto them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it ?
6.bsb: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”

6.web: He looked around at them all, and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did, and his hand was restored as sound as the other.
6.kjv: And looking round about upon them all, he said unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
6.bsb: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored.

6.web: But they were filled with rage, and talked with one another about what they might do to Jesus.
6.kjv: And they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.
6.bsb: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.

6.web: In these days, he went out to the mountain to pray, and he continued all night in prayer to God.
6.kjv: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
6.bsb: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.

6.web: When it was day, he called his disciples, and from them he chose twelve, whom he also named apostles:
6.kjv: And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;
6.bsb: When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:

6.web: Simon, whom he also named Peter; Andrew, his brother; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;
6.kjv: Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
6.bsb: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;

6.web: Matthew; Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Simon, who was called the Zealot;
6.kjv: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
6.bsb: Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;

6.web: Judas the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who also became a traitor.
6.kjv: And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.
6.bsb: Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.

6.web: He came down with them, and stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples, and a great number of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases;
6.kjv: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judæa and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;
6.bsb: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.

6.web: as well as those who were troubled by unclean spirits, and they were being healed.
6.kjv: And they that were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed.
6.bsb: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.

6.web: All the multitude sought to touch him, for power came out of him and healed them all.
6.kjv: And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went virtue out of him, and healed them all.
6.bsb: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all.

6.web: He lifted up his eyes to his disciples, and said, “Blessed are you who are poor, God’s Kingdom is yours.
6.kjv: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.
6.bsb: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.

6.web: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
6.kjv: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.
6.bsb: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

6.web: Blessed are you when men shall hate you, and when they shall exclude and mock you, and throw out your name as evil, for the Son of Man’s sake.
6.kjv: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company , and shall reproach you , and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.
6.bsb: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.

6.web: Rejoice in that day, and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven, for their fathers did the same thing to the prophets.
6.kjv: Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.
6.bsb: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.

6.web: “But woe to you who are rich! For you have received your consolation.
6.kjv: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.
6.bsb: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.

6.web: Woe to you, you who are full now, for you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
6.kjv: Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.
6.bsb: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.

6.web: Woe, when men speak well of you, for their fathers did the same thing to the false prophets.
6.kjv: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
6.bsb: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.

6.web: “But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
6.kjv: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,
6.bsb: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

6.web: bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
6.kjv: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.
6.bsb: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.

6.web: To him who strikes you on the cheek, offer also the other; and from him who takes away your cloak, don’t withhold your coat also.
6.kjv: And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloke forbid not to take thy coat also.
6.bsb: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.

6.web: Give to everyone who asks you, and don’t ask him who takes away your goods to give them back again.
6.kjv: Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.
6.bsb: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.

6.web: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
6.kjv: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.
6.bsb: Do to others as you would have them do to you.

6.web: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
6.kjv: For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.
6.bsb: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.

6.web: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
6.kjv: And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same.
6.bsb: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.

6.web: If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, to receive back as much.
6.kjv: And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.
6.bsb: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.

6.web: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
6.kjv: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.
6.bsb: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.

6.web: “Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.
6.kjv: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
6.bsb: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

6.web: Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Set free, and you will be set free.
6.kjv: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:
6.bsb: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

6.web: “Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be given to you. For with the same measure you measure it will be measured back to you.”
6.kjv: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
6.bsb: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”

6.web: He spoke a parable to them. “Can the blind guide the blind? Won’t they both fall into a pit?
6.kjv: And he spake a parable unto them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?
6.bsb: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

6.web: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone when he is fully trained will be like his teacher.
6.kjv: The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect shall be as his master.
6.bsb: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.

6.web: Why do you see the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
6.kjv: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but perceivest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
6.bsb: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

6.web: Or how can you tell your brother, ‘Brother, let me remove the speck of chaff that is in your eye,’ when you yourself don’t see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck of chaff that is in your brother’s eye.
6.kjv: Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother’s eye.
6.bsb: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

6.web: For there is no good tree that produces rotten fruit; nor again a rotten tree that produces good fruit.
6.kjv: For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
6.bsb: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.

6.web: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For people don’t gather figs from thorns, nor do they gather grapes from a bramble bush.
6.kjv: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.
6.bsb: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.

6.web: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart brings out that which is good, and the evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart brings out that which is evil, for out of the abundance of the heart, his mouth speaks.
6.kjv: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.
6.bsb: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.

6.web: “Why do you call me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ and don’t do the things which I say?
6.kjv: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?
6.bsb: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but not do what I say?

6.web: Everyone who comes to me, and hears my words, and does them, I will show you who he is like.
6.kjv: Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like:
6.bsb: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:

6.web: He is like a man building a house, who dug and went deep, and laid a foundation on the rock. When a flood arose, the stream broke against that house, and could not shake it, because it was founded on the rock.
6.kjv: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.
6.bsb: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.

6.web: But he who hears, and doesn’t do, is like a man who built a house on the earth without a foundation, against which the stream broke, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great.”
6.kjv: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.
6.bsb: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”

7.web: After he had finished speaking in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
7.kjv: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
7.bsb: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.

7.web: A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was sick and at the point of death.
7.kjv: And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.
7.bsb: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.

7.web: When he heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant.
7.kjv: And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.
7.bsb: When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.

7.web: When they came to Jesus, they begged him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for you to do this for him,
7.kjv: And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:
7.bsb: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this,

7.web: for he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us.”
7.kjv: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.
7.bsb: for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”

7.web: Jesus went with them. When he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under my roof.
7.kjv: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:
7.bsb: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.

7.web: Therefore I didn’t even think myself worthy to come to you; but say the word, and my servant will be healed.
7.kjv: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.
7.bsb: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

7.web: For I also am a man placed under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
7.kjv: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it .
7.bsb: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes; and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”

7.web: When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turned and said to the multitude who followed him, “I tell you, I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel.”
7.kjv: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
7.bsb: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”

7.web: Those who were sent, returning to the house, found that the servant who had been sick was well.
7.kjv: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.
7.bsb: And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health.

7.web: Soon afterwards, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples, along with a great multitude, went with him.
7.kjv: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.
7.bsb: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.

7.web: Now when he came near to the gate of the city, behold, one who was dead was carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. Many people of the city were with her.
7.kjv: Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.
7.bsb: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.

7.web: When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said to her, “Don’t cry.”
7.kjv: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.
7.bsb: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, “Do not weep.”

7.web: He came near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, arise!”
7.kjv: And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
7.bsb: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”

7.web: He who was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he gave him to his mother.
7.kjv: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.
7.bsb: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.

7.web: Fear took hold of all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and, “God has visited his people!”
7.kjv: And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people.
7.bsb: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”

7.web: This report went out concerning him in the whole of Judea, and in all the surrounding region.
7.kjv: And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judæa, and throughout all the region round about.
7.bsb: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.

7.web: The disciples of John told him about all these things.
7.kjv: And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things.
7.bsb: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things.

7.web: John, calling to himself two of his disciples, sent them to Jesus, saying, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for another?”
7.kjv: And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
7.bsb: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”

7.web: When the men had come to him, they said, “John the Baptizer has sent us to you, saying, ‘Are you he who comes, or should we look for another?’”
7.kjv: When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?
7.bsb: When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’”

7.web: In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and to many who were blind he gave sight.
7.kjv: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many that were blind he gave sight.
7.bsb: At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.

7.web: Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John the things which you have seen and heard: that the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have good news preached to them.
7.kjv: Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.
7.bsb: So He replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.

7.web: Blessed is he who finds no occasion for stumbling in me.”
7.kjv: And blessed is he , whosoever shall not be offended in me.
7.bsb: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”

7.web: When John’s messengers had departed, he began to tell the multitudes about John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
7.kjv: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness for to see? A reed shaken with the wind?
7.bsb: After John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?

7.web: But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are gorgeously dressed, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.
7.kjv: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.
7.bsb: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.

7.web: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.
7.kjv: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.
7.bsb: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

7.web: This is he of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
7.kjv: This is he , of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
7.bsb: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’

7.web: “For I tell you, among those who are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptizer, yet he who is least in God’s Kingdom is greater than he.”
7.kjv: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
7.bsb: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”

7.web: When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they declared God to be just, having been baptized with John’s baptism.
7.kjv: And all the people that heard him , and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.
7.bsb: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged God’s justice. For they had received the baptism of John.

7.web: But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God, not being baptized by him themselves.
7.kjv: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.
7.bsb: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.

7.web: “To what then will I liken the people of this generation? What are they like?
7.kjv: And the Lord said, Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?
7.bsb: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?

7.web: They are like children who sit in the marketplace, and call to one another, saying, ‘We piped to you, and you didn’t dance. We mourned, and you didn’t weep.’
7.kjv: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.
7.bsb: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’

7.web: For John the Baptizer came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
7.kjv: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil.
7.bsb: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’

7.web: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Behold, a gluttonous man, and a drunkard; a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
7.kjv: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!
7.bsb: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

7.web: Wisdom is justified by all her children.”
7.kjv: But wisdom is justified of all her children.
7.bsb: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”

7.web: One of the Pharisees invited him to eat with him. He entered into the Pharisee’s house, and sat at the table.
7.kjv: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee’s house, and sat down to meat.
7.bsb: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.

7.web: Behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that he was reclining in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster jar of ointment.
7.kjv: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,
7.bsb: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.

7.web: Standing behind at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and she wiped them with the hair of her head, kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
7.kjv: And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.
7.bsb: As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair. Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume.

7.web: Now when the Pharisee who had invited him saw it, he said to himself, “This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what kind of woman this is who touches him, that she is a sinner.”
7.kjv: Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it , he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.
7.bsb: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him—for she is a sinner!”

7.web: Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” He said, “Teacher, say on.”
7.kjv: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And he saith, Master, say on.
7.bsb: But Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, Teacher,” he said.

7.web: “A certain lender had two debtors. The one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
7.kjv: There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.
7.bsb: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

7.web: When they couldn’t pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?”
7.kjv: And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?
7.bsb: When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?”

7.web: Simon answered, “He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
7.kjv: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he , to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.
7.bsb: “I suppose the one who was forgiven more,” Simon replied. “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said.

7.web: Turning to the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head.
7.kjv: And he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.
7.bsb: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.

7.web: You gave me no kiss, but she, since the time I came in, has not ceased to kiss my feet.
7.kjv: Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet.
7.bsb: You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.

7.web: You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.
7.kjv: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment.
7.bsb: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.

7.web: Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.”
7.kjv: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
7.bsb: Therefore I tell you, because her many sins have been forgiven, she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”

7.web: He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
7.kjv: And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven.
7.bsb: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”

7.web: Those who sat at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
7.kjv: And they that sat at meat with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgiveth sins also?
7.bsb: But those at the table began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”

7.web: He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
7.kjv: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.
7.bsb: And Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

8.web: Soon afterwards, he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good news of God’s Kingdom. With him were the twelve,
8.kjv: And it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God: and the twelve were with him,
8.bsb: Soon afterward, Jesus traveled from one town and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with Him,

8.web: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out;
8.kjv: And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,
8.bsb: as well as some women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,

8.web: and Joanna, the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward; Susanna; and many others; who served them from their possessions.
8.kjv: And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.
8.bsb: Joanna the wife of Herod’s household manager Chuza, Susanna, and many others. These women were ministering to them out of their own means.

8.web: When a great multitude came together, and people from every city were coming to him, he spoke by a parable.
8.kjv: And when much people were gathered together, and were come to him out of every city, he spake by a parable:
8.bsb: While a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from town after town, He told them this parable:

8.web: “The farmer went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the road, and it was trampled under foot, and the birds of the sky devoured it.
8.kjv: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.
8.bsb: “A farmer went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.

8.web: Other seed fell on the rock, and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.
8.kjv: And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away, because it lacked moisture.
8.bsb: Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture.

8.web: Other fell amid the thorns, and the thorns grew with it, and choked it.
8.kjv: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.
8.bsb: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings.

8.web: Other fell into the good ground, and grew, and produced one hundred times as much fruit.” As he said these things, he called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
8.kjv: And other fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bare fruit an hundredfold. And when he had said these things, he cried, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
8.bsb: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop—a hundredfold.” As Jesus said this, He called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

8.web: Then his disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”
8.kjv: And his disciples asked him, saying, What might this parable be?
8.bsb: Then His disciples asked Him what this parable meant.

8.web: He said, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of God’s Kingdom, but to the rest in parables; that ‘seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.’
8.kjv: And he said, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to others in parables; that seeing they might not see, and hearing they might not understand.
8.bsb: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to others I speak in parables, so that, ‘though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand.’

8.web: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
8.kjv: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
8.bsb: Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.

8.web: Those along the road are those who hear, then the devil comes, and takes away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
8.kjv: Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.
8.bsb: The seeds along the path are those who hear, but the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.

8.web: Those on the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but these have no root, who believe for a while, then fall away in time of temptation.
8.kjv: They on the rock are they , which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.
8.bsb: The seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away.

8.web: That which fell among the thorns, these are those who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of life, and bring no fruit to maturity.
8.kjv: And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.
8.bsb: The seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature.

8.web: Those in the good ground, these are those who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it tightly, and produce fruit with perseverance.
8.kjv: But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it , and bring forth fruit with patience.
8.bsb: But the seeds on good soil are those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop.

8.web: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container, or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.
8.kjv: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but setteth it on a candlestick, that they which enter in may see the light.
8.bsb: No one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.

8.web: For nothing is hidden, that will not be revealed; nor anything secret, that will not be known and come to light.
8.kjv: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.
8.bsb: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.

8.web: Be careful therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to him will be given; and whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he thinks he has.”
8.kjv: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he seemeth to have.
8.bsb: Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”

8.web: His mother and brothers came to him, and they could not come near him for the crowd.
8.kjv: Then came to him his mother and his brethren, and could not come at him for the press.
8.bsb: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see Him, but they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd.

8.web: Some people told him, “Your mother and your brothers stand outside, desiring to see you.”
8.kjv: And it was told him by certain which said, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.
8.bsb: He was told, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.”

8.web: But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God, and do it.”
8.kjv: And he answered and said unto them, My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it.
8.bsb: But He replied, “My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out.”

8.web: Now on one of those days, he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples, and he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side of the lake.” So they launched out.
8.kjv: Now it came to pass on a certain day, that he went into a ship with his disciples: and he said unto them, Let us go over unto the other side of the lake. And they launched forth.
8.bsb: One day Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So He got into a boat with them and set out.

8.web: But as they sailed, he fell asleep. A wind storm came down on the lake, and they were taking on dangerous amounts of water.
8.kjv: But as they sailed he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filled with water , and were in jeopardy.
8.bsb: As they sailed, He fell asleep, and a windstorm came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger.

8.web: They came to him, and awoke him, saying, “Master, master, we are dying!” He awoke, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they ceased, and it was calm.
8.kjv: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he arose, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm.
8.bsb: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!” Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and they subsided, and all was calm.

8.web: He said to them, “Where is your faith?” Being afraid they marveled, saying to one another, “Who is this then, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”
8.kjv: And he said unto them, Where is your faith? And they being afraid wondered, saying one to another, What manner of man is this! for he commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey him.
8.bsb: “Where is your faith?” He asked. Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!”

8.web: They arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
8.kjv: And they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is over against Galilee.
8.bsb: Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.

8.web: When Jesus stepped ashore, a certain man out of the city who had demons for a long time met him. He wore no clothes, and didn’t live in a house, but in the tombs.
8.kjv: And when he went forth to land, there met him out of the city a certain man, which had devils long time, and ware no clothes, neither abode in any house, but in the tombs.
8.bsb: When Jesus stepped ashore, He was met by a demon-possessed man from the town. For a long time this man had not worn clothing or lived in a house, but he stayed in the tombs.

8.web: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, “What do I have to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don’t torment me!”
8.kjv: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God most high? I beseech thee, torment me not.
8.bsb: When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before Him, shouting in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!”

8.web: For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For the unclean spirit had often seized the man. He was kept under guard, and bound with chains and fetters. Breaking the bonds apart, he was driven by the demon into the desert.
8.kjv: (For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For oftentimes it had caught him: and he was kept bound with chains and in fetters; and he brake the bands, and was driven of the devil into the wilderness.)
8.bsb: For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and been driven by the demon into solitary places.

8.web: Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” for many demons had entered into him.
8.kjv: And Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many devils were entered into him.
8.bsb: “What is your name?” Jesus asked. “Legion,” he replied, because many demons had gone into him.

8.web: They begged him that he would not command them to go into the abyss.
8.kjv: And they besought him that he would not command them to go out into the deep.
8.bsb: And the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss.

8.web: Now there was there a herd of many pigs feeding on the mountain, and they begged him that he would allow them to enter into those. He allowed them.
8.kjv: And there was there an herd of many swine feeding on the mountain: and they besought him that he would suffer them to enter into them. And he suffered them.
8.bsb: There on the hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding. So the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs, and He gave them permission.

8.web: The demons came out of the man, and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake, and were drowned.
8.kjv: Then went the devils out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked.
8.bsb: Then the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.

8.web: When those who fed them saw what had happened, they fled, and told it in the city and in the country.
8.kjv: When they that fed them saw what was done, they fled, and went and told it in the city and in the country.
8.bsb: When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside.

8.web: People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus, and found the man from whom the demons had gone out, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
8.kjv: Then they went out to see what was done; and came to Jesus, and found the man, out of whom the devils were departed, sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
8.bsb: So the people went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man whom the demons had left, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.

8.web: Those who saw it told them how he who had been possessed by demons was healed.
8.kjv: They also which saw it told them by what means he that was possessed of the devils was healed.
8.bsb: Meanwhile, those who had seen it reported how the demon-possessed man had been healed.

8.web: All the people of the surrounding country of the Gadarenes asked him to depart from them, for they were very much afraid. He entered into the boat, and returned.
8.kjv: Then the whole multitude of the country of the Gadarenes round about besought him to depart from them; for they were taken with great fear: and he went up into the ship, and returned back again.
8.bsb: Then all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them. So He got into the boat and started back.

8.web: But the man from whom the demons had gone out begged him that he might go with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,
8.kjv: Now the man out of whom the devils were departed besought him that he might be with him: but Jesus sent him away, saying,
8.bsb: The man whom the demons had left begged to go with Jesus. But He sent him away, saying,

8.web: “Return to your house, and declare what great things God has done for you.” He went his way, proclaiming throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.
8.kjv: Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee. And he went his way, and published throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done unto him.
8.bsb: “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” So the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.

8.web: When Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
8.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when Jesus was returned, the people gladly received him: for they were all waiting for him.
8.bsb: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him, for they had all been waiting for Him.

8.web: Behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue. He fell down at Jesus’ feet, and begged him to come into his house,
8.kjv: And, behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue: and he fell down at Jesus’ feet, and besought him that he would come into his house:
8.bsb: Just then a synagogue leader named Jairus came and fell at Jesus’ feet. He begged Him to come to his house,

8.web: for he had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he went, the multitudes pressed against him.
8.kjv: For he had one only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she lay a dying. But as he went the people thronged him.
8.bsb: because his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying. As Jesus went with him, the crowds pressed around Him,

8.web: A woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her living on physicians, and could not be healed by any,
8.kjv: And a woman having an issue of blood twelve years, which had spent all her living upon physicians, neither could be healed of any,
8.bsb: including a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all her money on physicians, but no one was able to heal her.

8.web: came behind him, and touched the fringe of his cloak, and immediately the flow of her blood stopped.
8.kjv: Came behind him , and touched the border of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched.
8.bsb: She came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak, and immediately her bleeding stopped.

8.web: Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When all denied it, Peter and those with him said, “Master, the multitudes press and jostle you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
8.kjv: And Jesus said, Who touched me? When all denied, Peter and they that were with him said, Master, the multitude throng thee and press thee , and sayest thou, Who touched me?
8.bsb: “Who touched Me?” Jesus asked. But they all denied it. “Master,” said Peter, “the people are crowding and pressing against You.”

8.web: But Jesus said, “Someone did touch me, for I perceived that power has gone out of me.”
8.kjv: And Jesus said, Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue is gone out of me.
8.bsb: But Jesus declared, “Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.”

8.web: When the woman saw that she was not hidden, she came trembling, and falling down before him declared to him in the presence of all the people the reason why she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
8.kjv: And when the woman saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him, she declared unto him before all the people for what cause she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
8.bsb: Then the woman, seeing that she could not escape notice, came trembling and fell down before Him. In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed.

8.web: He said to her, “Daughter, cheer up. Your faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
8.kjv: And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.
8.bsb: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”

8.web: While he still spoke, one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house came, saying to him, “Your daughter is dead. Don’t trouble the Teacher.”
8.kjv: While he yet spake, there cometh one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house , saying to him, Thy daughter is dead; trouble not the Master.
8.bsb: While He was still speaking, someone arrived from the house of the synagogue leader. “Your daughter is dead,” he told Jairus. “Do not bother the Teacher anymore.”

8.web: But Jesus hearing it, answered him, “Don’t be afraid. Only believe, and she will be healed.”
8.kjv: But when Jesus heard it , he answered him, saying, Fear not: believe only, and she shall be made whole.
8.bsb: But Jesus overheard them and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”

8.web: When he came to the house, he didn’t allow anyone to enter in, except Peter, John, James, the father of the child, and her mother.
8.kjv: And when he came into the house, he suffered no man to go in, save Peter, and James, and John, and the father and the mother of the maiden.
8.bsb: When He entered the house, He did not allow anyone to go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother.

8.web: All were weeping and mourning her, but he said, “Don’t weep. She isn’t dead, but sleeping.”
8.kjv: And all wept, and bewailed her: but he said, Weep not; she is not dead, but sleepeth.
8.bsb: Meanwhile, everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said, “Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep.”

8.web: They were ridiculing him, knowing that she was dead.
8.kjv: And they laughed him to scorn, knowing that she was dead.
8.bsb: And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead.

8.web: But he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand, he called, saying, “Child, arise!”
8.kjv: And he put them all out, and took her by the hand, and called, saying, Maid, arise.
8.bsb: But Jesus took her by the hand and called out, “Child, get up!”

8.web: Her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately. He commanded that something be given to her to eat.
8.kjv: And her spirit came again, and she arose straightway: and he commanded to give her meat.
8.bsb: Her spirit returned, and at once she got up. And He directed that she be given something to eat.

8.web: Her parents were amazed, but he commanded them to tell no one what had been done.
8.kjv: And her parents were astonished: but he charged them that they should tell no man what was done.
8.bsb: Her parents were astounded, but Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.

9.web: He called the twelve together, and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.
9.kjv: Then he called his twelve disciples together, and gave them power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases.
9.bsb: Then Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to cure diseases.

9.web: He sent them out to preach God’s Kingdom and to heal the sick.
9.kjv: And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.
9.bsb: And He sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.

9.web: He said to them, “Take nothing for your journey—neither staffs, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money; neither have two coats each.
9.kjv: And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece.
9.bsb: “Take nothing for the journey,” He told them, “no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic.

9.web: Into whatever house you enter, stay there, and depart from there.
9.kjv: And whatsoever house ye enter into, there abide, and thence depart.
9.bsb: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area.

9.web: As many as don’t receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.”
9.kjv: And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.
9.bsb: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”

9.web: They departed, and went throughout the villages, preaching the Good News, and healing everywhere.
9.kjv: And they departed, and went through the towns, preaching the gospel, and healing every where.
9.bsb: So they set out and went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere.

9.web: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him; and he was very perplexed, because it was said by some that John had risen from the dead,
9.kjv: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him: and he was perplexed, because that it was said of some, that John was risen from the dead;
9.bsb: When Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, he was perplexed. For some were saying that John had risen from the dead,

9.web: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the old prophets had risen again.
9.kjv: And of some, that Elias had appeared; and of others, that one of the old prophets was risen again.
9.bsb: others that Elijah had appeared, and still others that a prophet of old had arisen.

9.web: Herod said, “John I beheaded, but who is this, about whom I hear such things?” He sought to see him.
9.kjv: And Herod said, John have I beheaded: but who is this, of whom I hear such things? And he desired to see him.
9.bsb: “I beheaded John,” Herod said, “but who is this man I hear such things about?” And he kept trying to see Jesus.

9.web: The apostles, when they had returned, told him what things they had done. He took them, and withdrew apart to a desert region of a city called Bethsaida.
9.kjv: And the apostles, when they were returned, told him all that they had done. And he took them, and went aside privately into a desert place belonging to the city called Bethsaida.
9.bsb: Then the apostles returned and reported to Jesus all that they had done. Taking them away privately, He withdrew to a town called Bethsaida.

9.web: But the multitudes, perceiving it, followed him. He welcomed them, and spoke to them of God’s Kingdom, and he cured those who needed healing.
9.kjv: And the people, when they knew it , followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.
9.bsb: But the crowds found out and followed Him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and He healed those who needed healing.

9.web: The day began to wear away; and the twelve came, and said to him, “Send the multitude away, that they may go into the surrounding villages and farms, and lodge, and get food, for we are here in a deserted place.”
9.kjv: And when the day began to wear away, then came the twelve, and said unto him, Send the multitude away, that they may go into the towns and country round about, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place.
9.bsb: As the day neared its end, the Twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions. For we are in a desolate place here.”

9.web: But he said to them, “You give them something to eat.” They said, “We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we should go and buy food for all these people.”
9.kjv: But he said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they said, We have no more but five loaves and two fishes; except we should go and buy meat for all this people.
9.bsb: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” “We have only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered, “unless we go and buy food for all these people.”

9.web: For they were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples, “Make them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
9.kjv: For they were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit down by fifties in a company.
9.bsb: (There were about five thousand men.) He told His disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”

9.web: They did so, and made them all sit down.
9.kjv: And they did so, and made them all sit down.
9.bsb: They did so, and everyone was seated.

9.web: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to the sky, he blessed them, and broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the multitude.
9.kjv: Then he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed them, and brake, and gave to the disciples to set before the multitude.
9.bsb: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples to set before the people.

9.web: They ate, and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
9.kjv: And they did eat, and were all filled: and there was taken up of fragments that remained to them twelve baskets.
9.bsb: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.

9.web: As he was praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he asked them, “Who do the multitudes say that I am?”
9.kjv: And it came to pass, as he was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?
9.bsb: One day as Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were with Him, He questioned them: “Who do the crowds say I am?”

9.web: They answered, “‘John the Baptizer,’ but others say, ‘Elijah,’ and others, that one of the old prophets is risen again.”
9.kjv: They answering said, John the Baptist; but some say , Elias; and others say , that one of the old prophets is risen again.
9.bsb: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, that a prophet of old has arisen.”

9.web: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
9.kjv: He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.
9.bsb: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”

9.web: But he warned them, and commanded them to tell this to no one,
9.kjv: And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing;
9.bsb: Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone.

9.web: saying, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.”
9.kjv: Saying, The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day.
9.bsb: “The Son of Man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”

9.web: He said to all, “If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
9.kjv: And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.
9.bsb: Then Jesus said to all of them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.

9.web: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake, the same will save it.
9.kjv: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.
9.bsb: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.

9.web: For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?
9.kjv: For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?
9.bsb: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?

9.web: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words, of him will the Son of Man be ashamed, when he comes in his glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.
9.kjv: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory, and in his Father’s, and of the holy angels.
9.bsb: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.

9.web: But I tell you the truth: There are some of those who stand here, who will in no way taste of death, until they see God’s Kingdom.”
9.kjv: But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.
9.bsb: But I tell you truthfully, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God.”

9.web: About eight days after these sayings, he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.
9.kjv: And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
9.bsb: About eight days after Jesus had said these things, He took with Him Peter, John, and James, and went up on a mountain to pray.

9.web: As he was praying, the appearance of his face was altered, and his clothing became white and dazzling.
9.kjv: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering.
9.bsb: And as He was praying, the appearance of His face changed, and His clothes became radiantly white.

9.web: Behold, two men were talking with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
9.kjv: And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:
9.bsb: Suddenly two men, Moses and Elijah, began talking with Jesus.

9.web: who appeared in glory, and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
9.kjv: Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
9.bsb: They appeared in glory and spoke about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.

9.web: Now Peter and those who were with him were heavy with sleep, but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men who stood with him.
9.kjv: But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.
9.bsb: Meanwhile Peter and his companions were overcome by sleep, but when they awoke, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with Him.

9.web: As they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let’s make three tents: one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah,” not knowing what he said.
9.kjv: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.
9.bsb: As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” (He did not know what he was saying.)

9.web: While he said these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered into the cloud.
9.kjv: While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.
9.bsb: While Peter was speaking, a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.

9.web: A voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
9.kjv: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
9.bsb: And a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”

9.web: When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They were silent, and told no one in those days any of the things which they had seen.
9.kjv: And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.
9.bsb: After the voice had spoken, only Jesus was present with them. The disciples kept this to themselves, and in those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen.

9.web: On the next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a great multitude met him.
9.kjv: And it came to pass, that on the next day, when they were come down from the hill, much people met him.
9.bsb: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, Jesus was met by a large crowd.

9.web: Behold, a man from the crowd called out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only child.
9.kjv: And, behold, a man of the company cried out, saying, Master, I beseech thee, look upon my son: for he is mine only child.
